record.paper_title: Global results on rational systems in the plane, part 1
record.context_brief: local stability versus global attractivity for second-order rational equations
record.original_question: For the second-order rational difference equation x_{n+1} = (a + b x_n + g x_{n-1})/(A + B x_n + C x_{n-1}), with nonnegative parameters and positive initial conditions for which the denominator is always positive, prove or disprove that local asymptotic stability of an equilibrium implies global attractivity of that equilibrium. Equivalently, for the first-order planar system x_{n+1} = (a + b x_n + g y_n)/(A + B x_n + C y_n), y_{n+1} = x_n, under the same nonnegative-parameter and positive-initial-condition assumptions, determine whether local asymptotic stability of an equilibrium implies global attractivity.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the second-order rational difference equation
  x_{n+1} = (a + b x_n + g x_{n-1}) / (A + B x_n + C x_{n-1}),  n = 0, 1, 2, ...,
where the parameters a, b, g, A, B, C are nonnegative real numbers and the initial conditions x_{-1}, x_0 are positive numbers chosen so that the denominator A + B x_n + C x_{n-1} is positive for every n ≥ 0. Equivalently, view this as a planar first-order system
  x_{n+1} = (a + b x_n + g y_n) / (A + B x_n + C y_n),
  y_{n+1} = x_n,
with (x_0, y_0) in the positive quadrant such that all iterates are well-defined.

An equilibrium is a point x̄ > 0 satisfying x̄ = (a + b x̄ + g x̄)/(A + B x̄ + C x̄). Such an equilibrium is locally asymptotically stable if the linearization at the corresponding fixed point (x̄, x̄) of the planar map has both eigenvalues of modulus less than 1. The equilibrium is a global attractor if every positive solution (with well-defined iterates) converges to x̄.

Prove or disprove: for every choice of nonnegative parameters (a, b, g, A, B, C) (with the system non-degenerate so that solutions exist), local asymptotic stability of an equilibrium of this equation implies that the equilibrium is a global attractor of all positive solutions.
artifact.status_search_result: This is a long-standing conjecture of Kulenović and Ladas (often phrased "when does local asymptotic stability imply global attractivity in rational equations?", Camouzis–Ladas 2006). It has been resolved affirmatively for many special parametric subcases of the second-order rational equation, and several recent papers claim complete proofs for particular families of conjectures of this form, but a fully general resolution covering all admissible nonnegative-parameter choices does not appear to be established. The status is best described as partially solved with many cases settled.

status_evidence.title: When does local asymptotic stability imply global attractivity in rational equations?
status_evidence.snippet: Camouzis and Ladas study precisely the conjecture that local asymptotic stability implies global attractivity for rational difference equations.
status_evidence.claim: The question is an explicit conjecture by Camouzis and Ladas, indicating its status as an open conjecture with partial results.

status_evidence.title: Global Dynamics of a Rational Difference Equation and Its Solutions to Several Conjectures
status_evidence.snippet: Recent paper proves global attractivity results that solve several conjectures of Kulenović–Ladas type.
status_evidence.claim: Numerous special cases of the conjecture have been resolved, but the general conjecture remains a guiding open problem.
